Package com.salesforce.multicloudj.pubsub.ali

Class AliBaseTopic<T extends AliBaseTopic<T>>

java.lang.Object
com.salesforce.multicloudj.pubsub.driver.AbstractTopic<T>
com.salesforce.multicloudj.pubsub.ali.AliBaseTopic<T>
All Implemented Interfaces:
Provider, SdkService, AutoCloseable
Direct Known Subclasses:
AliSmqQueue, AliSmqTopic
public abstract class AliBaseTopic<T extends AliBaseTopic<T>> extends AbstractTopic<T>
Abstract base for Alibaba SMQ (MNS) topic (publisher) implementations.

Holds the logic shared by every SMQ publisher: converting a multicloudj Message into the SMQ SDK message (toSmqMessage(com.salesforce.multicloudj.pubsub.driver.Message)), the batch limits (createBatcherOptions()), and error translation (mapException(java.lang.Throwable)). Concrete subclasses implement doSendBatch with the queue- or topic-specific SMQ call.

      public void close() throws Exception

    • createBatcherOptions

      protected Batcher.Options createBatcherOptions()
      Overrides the default batcher options to align with SMQ service limits.

      Only the 16-message count cap is set here. The byte-size cap is left disabled (0) because the batcher cannot size the driver Message it accumulates; the aggregate byte limit is instead enforced in the publish path by splitBySize(java.util.List<com.salesforce.multicloudj.pubsub.driver.Message>).

      Overrides:
      createBatcherOptions in class AbstractTopic<T extends AliBaseTopic<T>>

    • measureWireSize

      protected long measureWireSize(Message message)
      Returns a conservative upper bound on the SMQ wire size of message: the serialized body (base64-encoded or raw XML text, per the configured AliBaseTopic.Base64EncodingStrategy), a fixed per-message XML envelope allowance, the serialized size of the message metadata carried as SMQ user properties, and — when the body is base64-encoded — the reserved base64 flag property.

      Isolated as a pure size function so it can later be handed to the shared batcher as a per-provider sizer instead of being enforced here.

    • shouldBase64EncodeBody

      protected boolean shouldBase64EncodeBody(byte[] body)
      Whether the body is base64-encoded on the wire for the configured strategy: always under AliBaseTopic.Base64EncodingStrategy.ALWAYS, and under AliBaseTopic.Base64EncodingStrategy.AUTO only when the body is not XML-safe UTF-8 — that is, when it is not valid UTF-8 or contains an XML-illegal control byte, neither of which can be carried losslessly as raw XML text.

    • ensureWithinRequestSizeLimit

      protected long ensureWithinRequestSizeLimit(Message message)
      Fails fast with InvalidArgumentException if this single message, together with the fixed per-request overhead, exceeds MAX_REQUEST_BYTE_SIZE — such a message could never be sent in any batch. Returns the message's measured wire size so callers can reuse it without re-measuring.

    • splitBySize

      protected List<List<Message>> splitBySize(List<Message> messages)
      Packs an already count-capped (<= MAX_BATCH_SIZE) list into sub-batches whose estimated request size (FIXED_REQUEST_OVERHEAD_BYTES plus the cumulative wire size of the messages) stays within MAX_REQUEST_BYTE_SIZE, the 64 KB (65,536 bytes) total payload per batch that SMQ BatchSendMessage documents.

      Fails fast with InvalidArgumentException if any single message, together with the fixed per-request overhead, exceeds the limit on its own, since such a message can never be sent in any batch. The packing loop is kept self-contained so it could later be lifted into the shared batcher alongside a per-provider sizer.

    • mapException

      public SubstrateSdkException mapException(Throwable t)
      Description copied from interface: SdkService
      Maps a provider-specific Throwable to a fully-built SubstrateSdkException the caller can throw directly. The returned exception carries both the typed mapping (e.g. ResourceNotFoundException for HTTP 404) and an authoritative retryable flag derived from the native cloud SDK signal (e.g. AWS throttling, GCP ApiException.isRetryable(), status codes), or the type's default retryability when the SDK exposes no native signal.

      Callers throw the result; they do not inspect or transform it further: 

      
 try {
   ...
 } catch (Throwable t) {
   throw provider.mapException(t);
 }

      Implementation contract: implementations should compute a typed exception class (typically via their per-service ErrorCodeMapping) and a retryable hint, then return ExceptionHandler.build(exceptionClass, t, retryableHint). Implementations do not need to short-circuit when t is already a SubstrateSdkException: ExceptionHandler.build preserves an already-mapped exception's concrete subtype and retryable flag.

      Parameters:
      t - the original throwable from the provider SDK
      Returns:
      a built SubstrateSdkException ready to throw

    • toSmqMessage

      protected com.aliyun.mns.model.Message toSmqMessage(Message message)
      Converts a multicloudj Message into an SMQ SDK message.

      The body is placed on the wire per the configured AliBaseTopic.Base64EncodingStrategy: as base64 (Message.MessageBodyType.BASE64) or as raw XML text (Message.MessageBodyType.RAW_STRING). When base64 is applied, the reserved RESERVED_BASE64_FLAG_KEY user property is set so the receiver knows to base64-decode the body.

      Message metadata is mapped onto SMQ user properties natively: each entry's key is escaped to the SMQ attribute-name charset, and its value is carried as a PropertyType.STRING property when XML-safe or a PropertyType.BINARY property otherwise (a null value is first coalesced to the empty string). The per-message limits (at most MAX_USER_PROPERTIES attributes, each value at most MAX_PROPERTY_VALUE_LENGTH characters, each encoded key at most MAX_USER_PROPERTY_KEY_LENGTH characters) are enforced fail-fast here so an over-limit message is rejected before publish; when the body is base64-encoded the reserved flag occupies one of those attribute slots, so the effective metadata cap is one lower.

    • stampsTopicOriginatedMarker

      protected boolean stampsTopicOriginatedMarker()
      Whether this publisher stamps the reserved RESERVED_TOPIC_ORIGINATED_KEY marker on every message — topic publishers do (so the subscription can tell a topic delivery from a direct message authoritatively); the queue publisher does not. When true the marker is an always-present reserved user property, so the shared cap check (toUserProperties(java.util.Map<java.lang.String, java.lang.String>, boolean, boolean)) and size accounting (measureWireSize(com.salesforce.multicloudj.pubsub.driver.Message)) each reserve one slot for it. The marker itself is stamped by the topic publisher, not here.

    • buildUserProperties

      protected Map<String,com.aliyun.mns.model.MessagePropertyValue> buildUserProperties(Map<String,String> metadata, boolean base64)
      Assembles the native SMQ user-property map an outbound message carries: the metadata properties (with the per-message limits enforced fail-fast) plus, when the body is base64-encoded, the reserved RESERVED_BASE64_FLAG_KEY flag so the receiver knows to base64-decode the body.

      Returns null when there is nothing to carry — no metadata and no base64 flag — so the caller can skip setting an empty user-property map on the SMQ message. Each always-present reserved flag (the base64 body flag when base64-encoded, and — on the topic path — the RESERVED_TOPIC_ORIGINATED_KEY marker) reserves one of SMQ's MAX_USER_PROPERTIES attribute slots, so toUserProperties enforces the correspondingly lower metadata cap before those flags are added. The base64 flag is added here; the topic marker is added by the topic publisher.

      Parameters:
      metadata - the message metadata to map onto user properties, or null
      base64 - whether the body is base64-encoded, which adds the reserved flag property
      Throws:
      InvalidArgumentException - if the metadata exceeds the SMQ per-message limits (see toUserProperties(java.util.Map<java.lang.String, java.lang.String>, boolean, boolean))
